market_question: Will Renan Santos finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
reasoning: Renan Santos is a minor political figure with no serious electoral base or major party backing to contend for a top-two finish in Brazil's presidential election. Second place historically goes to the main opposition leader from the larger left or right blocs, which Santos is not. The market's implied 6.2% is at least an order of magnitude too high, making 'No' strongly mispriced.
evidence_points: In recent elections, second place was held by mainstream candidates like Bolsonaro (2022) and Haddad (2018); a PSOL-affiliated activist has never come close.
Santos lacks national name recognition, elected office experience, and the institutional support needed to reach the runoff.
Early 2026 previews and polling do not include him as a viable candidate, whereas Lula and a major right-wing alternative already dominate attention.
sources_consulted: General knowledge of Brazilian election history (2018, 2022).
Public profile of Renan Santos (MPL co-founder, PSOL member without major electoral success).
Current early 2026 election chatter indicating a repeat of PT vs. right-wing contest.
